7	
8	You design Minecraft builds the way a skilled human builder does, and you can see them: the toolkit renders
9	structure `.nbt` files headlessly with the game's real block models, so **every design decision gets checked by
10	looking**. This doctrine comes from a long measured study (concept→doc→build→revise pipelines, a facade
11	benchmark, a failed mesh-to-voxel detour, and decor work on a real procedural redstone town). Follow it.

14	Minecraft client jar from Mojang once and caches it). Details: [references/toolkit.md](references/toolkit.md).

16	## The five rules that decide the look
17	
18	1. **Design first; decorate never.** The ugliest results come from decoration applied to a form someone else
19	   (an algorithm, a redstone layout) already fixed: trim on a box is still a box. The best results come from
20	   deciding the *form* — massing, roof, openings, depth — as a designer. If you are asked to "decorate" a plain
21	   build, you are allowed (expected) to change its form wherever function and the user's constraints allow.
22	2. **Function is a contract, not an afterthought.** Whatever must keep working (redstone, rails, doors, walk
23	   paths, reserved machine space, street clearances) is written down as hard constraints *before* designing,
24	   and checked by code after (`mcd check before after`). A design pass that respects a written contract stays
25	   bold without breaking anything; one that guesses either breaks function or gets timid. See
26	   [references/function-contract.md](references/function-contract.md).
27	3. **Name the blocker; don't settle.** When the look you need is blocked by a contract term (a visible
28	   placeholder block, a no-projection rule, a reserved volume), say exactly which term and what it costs, so the
29	   owner can trade it. Quietly delivering half the design is the failure mode.
30	4. **Author as code, one bay at a time.** Write a short generator script (`mcd new`) using the build library:
31	   design one bay as a function, tile it on the rhythm, mirror for symmetry. Typing coordinates is where time
32	   and errors go; code makes cost scale with design decisions, not block count. **Curves and massing come from
33	   shape brushes**, never hand-placed blocks: `dome`, `cylinder`, `minaret`, `arch`
34	   ([references/shapes-curved.md](references/shapes-curved.md)); `setbacks`, `gableRoof`, `hipRoof`, `fins`,
35	   `parapet`, `cornice`, `falseFront`, `stepGable` ([references/shapes-massing.md](references/shapes-massing.md)).
36	   Hand-placed domes and setbacks came out faceted, too small, or as a flat box with a decorated front.
37	   **Roofs come from `mcd roof` / `roof()` by style name** (gable, hip, pyramid, mansard, gambrel, flat-parapet,
38	   shed, dutch-gable; with eaves, cornice, dormers, pediment, crest, chimneys, a tower): [references/roofs.md](references/roofs.md).
39	   **The site is part of the design**: terrain, sedimentary ledges, boulders, streams and waterfalls, woods, paths
40	   and bridges come from the landscaping brushes ([references/landscaping.md](references/landscaping.md)), checked
41	   with `mcd check --site`.
42	5. **Judge from where a person stands, and keep the better.** Render after every pass and *look* (Read the
43	   PNGs). Judge streets from eye height, interiors from inside (`--eye/--look`), never only from a flat
44	   elevation. A second pass is a coin flip unless you compare it to the first and keep the better one.

48	| Mode | When | Output |

51	| **Beautify an instance** (`/minecraft-design:beautify`) | a specific plain build exists (`.nbt`): an operator room, a hallway, a house | new `.nbt` (never overwrite) + before/after sheet + check report |
52	| **Type program** (`/minecraft-design:program`) | buildings come from a generator (procedural town, street of templates) — hand-editing one instance gets overwritten | a parametric generator module + contract + sheets on several instances |
53	| **Review** (`/minecraft-design:render`, `/minecraft-design:check`) | look at or audit any build | sheets, check report |
54	| **Build** (`/minecraft-design:build`, experimental) | good-at-a-glance builds from a one-line brief, unattended | `.nbt` + card, every version kept; revise with a comment ([references/build-workflow.md](references/build-workflow.md)) |

57	best one is a designed type program the generator places — not trim knobs on its massing (measured: trim on
58	fixed massing barely registers; a design-first type reads as a real building).

60	## The design procedure (all modes)
61	
62	1. **Read** the build and its context. `mcd info`, `mcd check`, `mcd render` — look at the sheet. What is it
63	   for, where does it sit (biome, neighbours, base materials, era), who uses it, what must keep working?
64	2. **Write the contract** (function, envelope, clearances, footprint) — from the build, the user, or the host
65	   project's rules. Unknown host rules are worth one look in the host repo before designing.
66	3. **Write a design brief** (≤200 words, in your reasoning or `brief.md`):
67	   - **Identity** in one line, from context — *never default to generic medieval cobble-and-oak*.
68	   - **Palette by role**: dominant ~60%, supporting ~30%, accent ~10%, 3–6 blocks, a named relationship
69	     ("dark timber / ochre render / grey stone"), each with a diegetic reason (what this place is built of).
70	     Colour needs a reason, not permission. Check contrast — trim that doesn't contrast doesn't read.
71	   - **Massing & roof**: the volumes and roof forms, their edges (verges, eaves, ridges).
72	   - **Rhythm**: bay width and what repeats in each bay.
73	   - **Base / middle / top**: plinth / body / cornice-roofline outside; floor / walls / ceiling inside.
74	   - **Depth plan**: what stands proud (+1/+2) and what recesses (−1/−2).
75	   - Optional: `mcd concept` for concept art when `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set — a strong craft reference.
76	4. **Build as code** (`mcd new build.mjs [--from in.nbt]`), in fenced passes, rendering after each:
77	   1. *Form*: massing, roof, openings — the part decoration can never fix later. Use the shape brushes; check
78	      the silhouette in the 3/4 view against the concept before any detail.
79	   2. *Structure & depth*: frames, posts, beams, piers proud of the wall; panels and openings recessed.
80	   3. *Materials* by role.
81	   4. *Detail*: sub-block pieces carry the craft (see [references/craft.md](references/craft.md)). Detail is its own
82	      phase, after the form is final, and can go to a cheap subagent: rules on face maps (`mcd faces`, `mcd paint`,
83	      [references/detail-language.md](references/detail-language.md)) or operations on named features
84	      (`mcd features`, `mcd detail`, [references/detailing.md](references/detailing.md)). Keep the undetailed build
85	      if the detail reads busier rather than better (texture mixes are the usual culprit). Ready-made craft brushes
86	      (plaque, signboard, bunting, profiled pilasters, surrounds, glazing, weather/vary presets, fixtures, planters,
87	      railing, finial, louvres, brackets) and roof PRESETS (`mcd roof --preset cottage|shop|townhouse|civic|temple|

89	   5. *Inspect before you finish*: `mcd check` (floating, unsupported, orphan blocks), `mcd palette` (roof/trim

94	   sheet. Fix the largest remaining blank surface (the check lists them). Revert a pass that made it worse.
95	6. **Report** (≤10 lines): identity, palette, what changed, contract result, any blocker terms named, files.
96	
97	## Calibration (what we measured)
98	
99	- Raise the bar, never cap: models under-detail to whatever bar they infer. Ask for showcase depth.
100	- One pass can't push every dimension; a "more detail" push drowned colour. Fence the passes.
101	- First drafts over-decorate (bands on every floor read as stripes; every-other-course quoins read as a
102	  checkerboard). Restraint — one strong line, paired quoins, rest areas — wins on the glance.
103	- Relief is construction, not recolour: swapping a wall's block is not detail; things standing proud are.
104	- Recess by exclusion: there is no "air op" in your head — carve a niche by *not placing* the wall block, and
105	  remember a recess in a 1-thick wall opens to whatever is behind it (back it).
106	- A rule that fails first: before trusting a protection, break it on purpose and watch the check catch it.
107	- Don't trust self-reported effort or time; measure. Don't trust a single numeric judge; compare pairwise.
108

110

112	Use **Opus 5.5** for final passes and long reference-heavy builds; **Haiku 5.5** (default effort) for cheap drafts and

2

5	tried before it: parallel Haiku fix-up tasks (4-1) and taste-profile revision rounds (3-0; the rounds pushed "fewer
6	colours, more weathering" and stripped the colour the owner liked), which cost 2-4x more.
7	
8	A concept image is inspiration, not a fidelity target. The workflow is a typed BAML program (`baml_src/ns_workflow/`)
9	packed into one executable; the model work goes through `claude -p` on the user's Claude plan, the card through `mcd`.
10	
11	| Command | Who | Writes |

10	  and `mcd convert` write either, by extension. Block-entity data and entities survive both ways.

14	- Walking into a building that faces north, you face **south (+z)**; east (+x) is on your **left**.
15	- `facing` on blocks:
16	  - **stairs**: the side of the full-height back. A cornice/bracket whose lip points at the street:
17	    `half: "top"`, `facing` = the direction *into* the wall. A roof slope rising to the north: `facing: "north"`.
18	  - **trapdoor**: the side it hinges from when open; closed `half: "top"` sits in the top of the cell.
19	  - **wall torch / wall sign / wall banner**: the direction it *points out* (away from the wall).
20	  - **repeater / comparator**: `facing` points toward the *input* (signal flows the opposite way).
21	  - **logs**: `axis: x|y|z`.
22	- `mcd states <block>` lists every valid property and value for a block in the target version; `mcd blocks
23	  --grep <re>` lists valid ids (ids change: 26.x renamed `chain` → `iron_chain`); `mcd blocks --check a,b,c` says

27	
28	| Command | Does |
29	|---|---|
30	| `render <f.nbt> [--out s.png] [--front d] [--ground y] [--cut y] [--eye x,y,z --look x,y,z [--label t]]... [--view "name:x,y,z->x,y,z"]... [--model m] [--raw]` | A builder's reference sheet (front elevation + 3/4, one scale, no scene). 56	shell(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", { floor: true, ceiling: false });
57	carve(g, a, b);                            // stores air (clears the cell on placement)
58	replace(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", "stone_bricks");

83	- **Signs:** their text, glowing text drawn brighter.

93	```

102	- **Standing `rotation`:** 0 faces south, 4 west, 8 north, 12 east. Wall banners and signs hang on the block behind
103	  them and face `facing`.

117	  *glance* tile (the street view at 320 px: what reads at a glance) and close-ups at ≥ 12 px per block of the
118	  entrance (door cells), the eave band, each facade's busiest region, and every small feature visible from outside
119	  (signs, banners, lanterns, pots, finials). Each tile is labelled with what it frames and its px/block; the JSON lists
120	  the box and side of each. For any other spot:
121	  `$MCD zoom house.nbt --at 12,3,0 [--radius 3] [--from n|s|e|w] [--out zoom.png]` (default side: the one with a clear

123	- **Change report** — `$MCD diff before.nbt after.nbt --png diff.png [--json] [--fail-empty]`: changed cells by kind

Render notes: no light engine (light sources show as blocks, not glow); interior eye views skip sun shadows;
block-entity blocks (chests, signs, beds, banners, heads) render as simple textured boxes; entities (item
frames, armour stands) are not drawn. Keep `--look` inside the build for interior views.

## Build library (`tools/src/build.mjs`)

```js
import { load, Grid, guard, tile, mirrorX, mirrorZ, shell, carve, replace, B, face, DIRS } from ".../tools/src/build.mjs";
const g = guard(load("in.nbt"));          // or: new Grid([w, h, d], { dataVersion })
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.stairs("dark_oak", "south", "top"));   // [block, state] helpers: stairs slab log wood trapdoor door fence wall lantern chain wallTorch pane block
g.fill([x0, y0, z0], [x1, y1, z1], "stone_bricks");
tile(g, { from: 1, step: 4, to: 19 }, (z, i) => bay(z, i));  // the bay rhythm
mirrorX(g, cx, (set) => set(x, y, z, block, state));          // symmetric pair, facings mirrored
shell(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", { floor: true, ceiling: false });
carve(g, a, b);                            // stores air (clears the cell on placement)
replace(g, a, b, "spruce_planks", "stone_bricks");
g.save("out.nbt");                          // never overwrite the input
console.log(g.refused);                     // guarded writes that were refused (report them)
```

Shape brushes (also exported from `build.mjs`): curved forms — `dome`, `cylinder`, `minaret`, `arch` (+ `circleCells`,
`ring`, `disc`, `revolve`) — see `shapes-curved.md`; massing — `setbacks`, `gableRoof`, `hipRoof`, `fins`, `parapet`,
`cornice`, `falseFront`, `stepGable` — see `shapes-massing.md`. Each is `fn(g, opts)`, writes through `g.set` (so
`guard()` still protects function), and returns `{cells, refused, bounds}`.

`guard(grid)` refuses writes into the grid's functional cells and their keep-clear cells (or a set you pass);
it never throws — check `g.refused`. `runParts(g, [["shell", shell.build], ["garden", garden.build]], { palette:
"palette.json" })` runs a build's parts in order so each can only add into air: writes into an earlier part's cells
(air included) are refused and reported, the ground laid before it stays writable, and blocks outside the palette
are reported per part. The Grid keeps block-entity NBT (sign text, chest contents) and entities and
writes them back unchanged; cells you don't touch round-trip byte-for-byte.

Grow the box with `g.resize([w, h, d], [dx, dy, dz])` (a shift grows toward −); a shift moves every coordinate,
so re-derive any contract coordinates after shifting.

## Banners, signs and other block entities

Banners, signs, chests, beds, bells, mob heads, decorated pots and shulker boxes are entity-rendered in vanilla, and
`mcd render` draws them with their entity models and textures:
- **Banners:** the cloth in its base colour plus every dyed pattern from the block entity.
- **Signs:** their text, glowing text drawn brighter.
- **Other entity-rendered blocks:** a neutral box, listed under `unknownBlocks` as "entity-rendered, approximated".

Author banners and signs with the build helpers. Each returns `[block, state, nbt]` with valid block-entity NBT
that round-trips through save and load:

```js
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("cyan", [["stripe_center", "white"], ["border", "black"]], { facing: "north" }));   // wall banner
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.banner("red", [["cross", "yellow"]], { wall: false, rotation: 8 }));                       // standing, faces north
g.set(x, y, z, ...B.sign("spruce", ["PERMIT", "OFFICE"], { facing: "north", color: "black", glow: false }));
```
- **Banner patterns:** `stripe_center`, `stripe_top`, `stripe_bottom`, `stripe_left`, `stripe_right`,
  `stripe_middle`, `border`, `curly_border`, `cross`, `straight_cross`, `rhombus`, `circle`, `flower`, `globe`,
  `gradient`, `gradient_up`, `half_horizontal`, `half_vertical`, `triangle_top`, `triangle_bottom`, `bricks`,
  `small_stripes`, `diagonal_left`, `diagonal_right` (the full list is under `textures/entity/banner/`).
- **Colours:** the 16 dye names.
- **NBT format:** banners use the 1.20.5+ `patterns` list (`legacy: true` writes the older `Patterns` /
  `Pattern` / `Color` form). Sign text is written as JSON components below data version 4325 (1.21.5) and as plain
  string components from 1.21.5 on (`dataVersion` option; the grid's default is 1.21.4).
- **Standing `rotation`:** 0 faces south, 4 west, 8 north, 12 east. Wall banners and signs hang on the block behind
  them and face `facing`.

## Review card

One image of a build for a glance or a reviewer (prints one JSON object; non-zero exit and a stderr message on error):

- `mcd card <f.nbt> --out card.png [--tiles dir] [--front n] [--reuse]` — render (close-ups, `MCD_TILE_SCALE=2`) and compose the card (street | front-left, front-right | back, plus the roof close-up row; tiles fit 700x700, white). `--reuse` skips the render when `dir/street.png` exists. `{"card","tiles","views":[...]}`
- `mcd card <f.nbt> --out eye.png --tiles dir --layout eye` — the eye-level card: only what a player sees from the ground (street | down-the-street left, right | back), sky trimmed, so a roof weighs what it weighs in the game.

## Inspection

Cheap, deterministic checks to run after every pass, before judging a render by eye. Each has `--json`.

- **Glance and close-ups** — `$MCD render house.nbt --closeups --tiles tiles/` adds a row of tiles to the sheet: a
  *glance* tile (the street view at 320 px: what reads at a glance) and close-ups at ≥ 12 px per block of the
  entrance (door cells), the eave band, each facade's busiest region, and every small feature visible from outside
  (signs, banners, lanterns, pots, finials). Each tile is labelled with what it frames and its px/block; the JSON lists
  the box and side of each. For any other spot:
  `$MCD zoom house.nbt --at 12,3,0 [--radius 3] [--from n|s|e|w] [--out zoom.png]` (default side: the one with a clear
  line of sight, front first; cells far in front of the spot are left out so they cannot hide it).
- **Change report** — `$MCD diff before.nbt after.nbt --png diff.png [--json] [--fail-empty]`: changed cells by kind
  (added / removed / replaced / state) and block, their groups and boxes, the faces they show on, how many are enclosed
  (never show) or interior-only; with `--png`, changed pixels per standard view and a BEFORE | AFTER pair cropped to
  the change for the two views that changed most. `--fail-empty` exits 1 when nothing changed, when no view shows a
  pixel of the change, or when every changed cell is enclosed — a pass that wrote nothing is a failure, not a no-op.
- **Palette** — `$MCD palette house.nbt`: visible blocks classed into roles by where they sit (walls field, trim and
  edges, roof, base, openings, accents, plants), each with its main materials and measured tone (texture average
  from the client jar). Flags, each with a concrete suggestion: roof in the walls' tone; trim invisible on its wall
  (`trim: stone_bricks on stone_bricks walls -> tuff_bricks or smooth_stone`); an outlier block used a handful of
  times that clashes with everything around it; more than 3 accent colour families; dark detail on a dark ground
  (or light on light).
- **Structure** — `$MCD check house.nbt` now always reports STRUCTURE: floating groups (not connected to the
  lowest layer through face or edge contact), unsupported hanging/mounted blocks (a hanging lantern with nothing
  above, a standing banner or lantern on air, a wall sign with nothing behind), orphans (one block sticking out
  sideways or dangling, touching the build on one face), and enclosed cells (a change there never shows; with two
  files, how many changed cells are enclosed). Report only; the exit code is unchanged.

1	# Roofs by style
2	
3	Roofs are where builds go wrong: flat caps, lumpy hips, stairs facing the wrong way. Don't place roof blocks by
4	hand. Choose a **style** and a few options, and the tool builds it. It gets stair facing, half and corner shapes
5	right at hips and valleys, closes steep faces, fills gable walls, and adds verges, eaves, ridge caps, dormers, a
6	pediment, chimneys and a tower. It works over a rectangle or a union of rectangles (L, T and U plans) and leaves the
7	inside hollow as an attic.
8	
9	```
10	mcd roof build.nbt --detect                                   # where is the eave, what is the footprint?
11	mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --style hip --pitch 45 --eave cornice --material deepslate_tiles --ridge crest
12	mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --spec roof.json                   # the same options as JSON
13	mcd compare build.nbt out.nbt --front n                       # look at it
14	```

17	roof(g, [[2, 2, 14, 10], [2, 11, 8, 16]], "hip", { y: 6, material: "deepslate_tile", eave: "cornice" });   // new build: y = wall top + 1
18	reroof(g, { style: "mansard", pitch: "steep", pediment: "north" });                                      // existing build

21	## Presets first
22	
23	A builder's own parameter choices for `mcd roof` kept producing the same failure: a low pitch, no overhang, no
24	ridge, and the roof in the wall material, so the roof read as a heavy lid that merged with the walls. **Start from a
25	preset.** Each one is good by construction and scales to the footprint:
26	- the pitch scales with the span;
27	- the overhang is 1 cell, or 2 on spans of 15 or more;
28	- dormer and chimney counts scale with the length;
29	- on walls of two storeys or less, the roof is never taller than the walls (cottage, shop and granary are steep by
30	  design).

32	```
33	mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --preset civic                     # flags override any preset field:
34	mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --preset townhouse --material dark_oak --front e

38	reroof(g, { preset: "civic" });

142	
143	- **`pitch`**:
144	  - `half`: slab steps, about 27°
145	  - `45`: stairs, 1:1
146	  - `steep`: stairs with full blocks, 2:1
147	  - `very-steep`: 3:1
148	  - or any number (rise per cell)
149	
150	  Eaves never drop more than one course per cell, so a steep roof does not swallow the top of the wall.
151	- **`overhang`** 0–2 (default 1). **`eave`**:
152	  - `plain`
153	  - `flared`: a half-pitch kick at the eave
154	  - `cornice`: a course of upside-down `trim` stairs under the eave, with dentils of alternating `trim` blocks under that
155	
156	  `soffit: true` (or a material) puts top slabs under a plain overhang.
157	- **Materials**:
158	  - `material` (the roof; any form of the name works: `deepslate_tiles`, `deepslate_tile`, `spruce`)
159	  - `trim` (cornice, dentils, tower band)
160	  - `gable` (the gable-end wall; default: the walls' own block)
161	  - `verge` (the barge course over each gable end)
162	  - `hips` (the hip stairs)
163	  - `pattern: {material, every, offset}` (banded courses)
164	- **`ridge`**:
165	  - `slab` (default for 45° and steeper): a half slab on the ridge
166	  - `wall`: a joined wall
167	  - `crest`: joined iron bars, the Victorian ridge crest
168	  - `rods`: end rods every other cell
169	  - `none`
170	  - or any block

172	  placed symmetrically on that face of the largest wing, keep clear of hip ends and the pediment, and step down or
173	  drop out where the main roof doesn't rise over them within four rows (so they never tunnel through it).
174	- **`pediment`**: `{face, width (55% of the face), pitch (45), tympanum, cornice (raking cornice material), oculus

176	  gable filled with `tympanum`, a raking cornice, and a small round window in the middle.
177	- **`chimneys`**: `[{at: [x,z], size, material, rise}]`. A chimney rises `rise` (2) above the roof top. A 1x1 chimney
178	  gets a smoking campfire on top, and bigger ones get slab caps.
179	- **`tower`**: `{at: [x,z], size (n or [w,d]), height (above the roof top), top: lantern|spire|cap, material}`. This
180	  is a hollow shaft through the roof with a band and small openings near the top, finished with one of:
181	  - `lantern`: corner posts, iron-bar railings, a hanging lantern, a small pyramid cap and a lightning-rod finial
182	  - `spire`: a 3:1 pyramid
183	  - `cap`: slab coping
184	- **`monitor`** (gable styles): a louvred vent along the middle 60% of the ridge. **`gableCornice`**: the cornice
185	  also runs across the gable ends (the base of a pediment). **`dentils: false`**: a slim cornice. **`rail`**

187	- **`keep`**: `[{from:[x,y,z], to:[x,y,z]}]`, cells never written or removed (a chimney or tower you want to keep).

189	  overhangs and height; the result's `shift` says how far everything moved.

191	## Re-roofing an existing build
192	
193	`reroof` and `mcd roof` work in three steps:
194	1. **Find the walls.** Tall columns are walls; the holes between them are filled to get the plan.
195	2. **Find the eave.** Each perimeter column's wall top is its highest solid with a mostly solid column beneath

# Roofs by style

Roofs are where builds go wrong: flat caps, lumpy hips, stairs facing the wrong way. Don't place roof blocks by
hand. Choose a **style** and a few options, and the tool builds it. It gets stair facing, half and corner shapes
right at hips and valleys, closes steep faces, fills gable walls, and adds verges, eaves, ridge caps, dormers, a
pediment, chimneys and a tower. It works over a rectangle or a union of rectangles (L, T and U plans) and leaves the
inside hollow as an attic.

```
mcd roof build.nbt --detect                                   # where is the eave, what is the footprint?
mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --style hip --pitch 45 --eave cornice --material deepslate_tiles --ridge crest
mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --spec roof.json                   # the same options as JSON
mcd compare build.nbt out.nbt --front n                       # look at it
```
```js
import { roof, reroof, detectEave } from "<plugin>/tools/src/build.mjs";
roof(g, [[2, 2, 14, 10], [2, 11, 8, 16]], "hip", { y: 6, material: "deepslate_tile", eave: "cornice" });   // new build: y = wall top + 1
reroof(g, { style: "mansard", pitch: "steep", pediment: "north" });                                      // existing build
```

## Presets first

A builder's own parameter choices for `mcd roof` kept producing the same failure: a low pitch, no overhang, no
ridge, and the roof in the wall material, so the roof read as a heavy lid that merged with the walls. **Start from a
preset.** Each one is good by construction and scales to the footprint:
- the pitch scales with the span;
- the overhang is 1 cell, or 2 on spans of 15 or more;
- dormer and chimney counts scale with the length;
- on walls of two storeys or less, the roof is never taller than the walls (cottage, shop and granary are steep by
  design).

```
mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --preset civic                     # flags override any preset field:
mcd roof build.nbt out.nbt --preset townhouse --material dark_oak --front e
```
```js
roof(g, rects, "cottage", { y });            // a preset name works as the style
reroof(g, { preset: "civic" });
```

| preset | the roof | good for |
|---|---|---|
| `cottage` | steep gable, `spruce-shingle` palette with dark oak verges, flared eaves, slab ridge, one chimney at a gable end | houses, cottages, rural buildings |
| `shop` | steep front gable (gable end to the street), `spruce-shingle` with spruce verges; side dormers on spans of 13+ | shopfronts, market buildings |
| `townhouse` | `dark-slate` mansard with dormers on the street face, stone cornice with dentils, iron-bar crest | row houses, Second Empire blocks |
| `civic` | 45-degree hip in the `slate` palette, quartz dentil cornice, a quartz pediment over the front | banks, halls, offices |
| `temple` | low gable to the front, `red-tile` palette, quartz raking cornice and tympanum, the cornice carried across the pediment's base | colonnades, porticos, museums |
| `granary` (`industrial`) | tall `slate` gable with a louvred monitor along the middle of the ridge | barns, granaries, workshops |
| `modern` (`flat-parapet-modern`) | parapet, smooth stone coping, a slim cornice without dentils, iron-bar rooftop rail | modern and commercial blocks |
| `barn` | gambrel along the long axis (break at 40% of the span, 1.5 then 0.5), `barn-red`, quartz barge boards, 2 dormers per long side (3 on 18+), a lantern cupola on the ridge | barns, stables, farm sheds |
| `teahouse` (`pagoda`) | low dutch gable, pitch 0.67, upturned eave corners with rafter tails, dark glazed tiles, stone ridge; the roof stays under 0.6 of the wall height | tea houses, shrines, East Asian pavilions |
| `tower-cap` | cone at 2.75:1 with a concave flare and a finial, a dormer on towers 7+ wide (override `material: copper` for a verdigris cap) | wizard towers, keeps, turrets |
| `lantern-cap` | shallow cone (1.25:1) with a ring course and finial | lighthouse lanterns, gazebos, bell cupolas |
| `church` (`stave`) | three stacked, steeper roofs (1, 1.5, 2) with a wall band and a window row between, dragon ridge ends, dark shingle mix | stave churches, pagodas, tiered halls |
| `workshop` | sawtooth: a row of sheds (one per 5 cells) with glazed north faces, `copper` in gap-free stairs and slabs | workshops, factories, studios |
| `desert` | flat sandstone deck, quartz coping, a wind tower | desert markets, adobe, flat-roofed villages |
| `cafe` | flat cantilever deck, overhang N2 S1 E1 W1, thin quartz fascia, spruce soffit, a vent stack | glass cafes, modern shopfronts with a canopy |

**Contrast** applies to presets and plain styles alike. If the roof material's measured tone is too close to the
dominant wall block (tone distance below 0.3, families.mjs colours), the preset's alternate material is used (or the
first that clears from the slate, spruce-shingle, dark-slate and red-tile palettes, dark oak, quartz, mud brick), and the result
`notes` say so. `contrast: false` (`--no-contrast`) keeps the material, for example a concept that wants dark slate
on dark walls. Overhang is always at least 1 unless you pass `overhang: 0`.

## Pick the preset by building type

Look the building up in the table above and use its preset on the first `mcd roof` call. Do not start from `--style`.
Quick map: house, cottage -> `cottage`; shopfront -> `shop`; row house -> `townhouse`; hall, bank -> `civic`; colonnade ->
`temple`; barn, stable -> `barn`; tea house, pagoda, shrine -> `teahouse`; round or square tower -> `tower-cap`; lighthouse
lantern -> `lantern-cap`; church, tiered hall -> `church`; factory, workshop -> `workshop`; desert, adobe -> `desert`; flat
cafe, modern block -> `cafe` or `modern`. `roof-review.mjs` has `SIZE_BUDGET` (wall courses and roof/wall ratio per type).

## Palettes: a roof is never one flat plane

`material` takes a **palette**, a single block (mixed automatically with two same-family neighbours) or your own
`{ mix: [[block, weight], ...], eave, ridge, verge, gradient, rows }`. Each palette is a weighted mix of 3+ visibly different
blocks, a darker eave course, a distinct ridge and verge. The default (no `material`) is `slate`, never one near-black
block. `--texture <palette>` / `texture: false` (one flat block: needs a reason, see below).

| palette | mix | use for |
|---|---|---|
| `slate` (default) | cobbled deepslate, deepslate tile, polished deepslate; blackstone-brick eave, stone-brick ridge | civic, general |
| `dark-slate` | deepslate tile with cobbled, blackstone and cracked-tile accents | townhouses, dark Gothic |
| `spruce-shingle` | spruce, dark oak, mangrove; dark oak eave, birch verge | cottages, shops |
| `red-tile` | brick, granite, polished granite, mangrove; mud-brick eave, quartz verge | temples, Mediterranean |
| `barn-red` | mangrove, brick, dark oak; dark oak eave, quartz verge | barns |
| `copper` | weathered and oxidized cut copper in rows; exposed eave, cut-copper ridge | towers, workshops, coastal |
| `dark-glazed` | deepslate tile, cobbled deepslate, blackstone brick; quartz ridge | East Asian tiles |
| `sandstone-deck` | smooth sandstone, cut sandstone, sandstone; quartz coping | flat desert roofs |

## Guard rails and `--dry-run`

Run `mcd roof in.nbt --preset <name> --dry-run` FIRST (a dry run writes nothing). It prints the roof report (wall and roof
height, ratio and its cap, overhang, tones, breaks) and every warning with a fix. Fix each warning, then run it for real. The
same warnings come back after a real run in `notes`, and `--strict` exits 2 on any.

| warning | meaning | fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ROOF_CONTRAST_OFF` | `--no-contrast` | drop it; choose a palette 0.3+ in tone from the walls |
| `ROOF_NO_OVERHANG` | a side has overhang 0 | overhang 1 (2 on spans of 15+); shorten the walls to fit a size cap |
| `ROOF_SINGLE_MATERIAL` | under 3 visible tones or `--texture none` | a palette or a 3+ block mix |
| `ROOF_TOO_TALL` | roof / wall ratio over the cap (0.6 on walls of 5 or less, 1.0 up to 9, 1.8 for cottage, barn, cone, church) | lower the pitch, raise the walls, a steep-by-design preset |
| `ROOF_LOW_PITCH` | pitch under 0.5 | pitch 0.5+ (0.67 only with `eave: upturned`) |
| `ROOF_BIG_PLANE` | an unbroken slope 10+ long | dormers, chimney, cross-gable, monitor, or gambrel / mansard |
| `ROOF_NO_RIDGE` | bare ridge seam | `ridge: slab` (crest on a mansard) |
| `ROOF_BLACK_LID` | near-black roof barely lighter than the walls | slate grey or a warm palette |
| `ROOF_DORMER_DROPPED` | a dormer did not fit | a longer face (7+), or another break |

**The bypass rule.** Never bypass a guard rail (`--no-contrast`, `--overhang 0`, `--texture none`, a pitch under 0.5)
without `--why "<reason that cites the concept image>"`, for example `--why "concept: black tiled roof on black timber walls"`.
Without a reason the tool refuses (CLI) or warns (library); with one it records the reason as a look note. "To fit the size
cap" is not a reason: shorten the walls. Forms with no eave by design (sawtooth, dome) are exempt automatically.

## Forms beyond a pitched plane

`--style cone | dome | onion | tiered | sawtooth` (or the presets above) build curved, stacked and glazed roofs:
`cone` (`pitch`, `lean`, `finial`, `dormer`), `dome`/`onion` (`drum`, `ribs`, finial; radius under 4 falls back to a cone),
`tiered` (`tiers`, `skirt`, `inset`, `band`, `pitches`), `sawtooth` (`bays`, `glaze`). `eave: upturned` lifts the corners of a
dutch gable or hip like a pagoda; `overhang` may be `{north, south, east, west}`; `maxHeight` caps the roof in courses (with no
explicit pitch the roof is capped at its ratio cap). `mcd render --closeups` includes a roof close-up tile so the texture is visible.
`examples/roofs/regression.png` shows the eight reference cases (`node examples/roofs/regression.mjs`).

`examples/roofs/presets.png` shows every preset on a small 9x7 shop and a 23x17 civic block
(`node examples/roofs/presets.mjs`).

## Styles (the raw options)

`examples/roofs/gallery.png` shows every style on the same L-plan house (`node examples/roofs/gallery.mjs`).

| style | what it is | good for |
|---|---|---|
| `gable` | two slopes per wing; ridges along each wing's long side, cross-gables meeting in valleys; gable walls filled with the wall block | cottages, barns, row houses (`ridgeAxis` to turn the ridge) |
| `hip` | slopes on every side; true hips (outer stairs) and valleys (inner stairs) on any rectilinear plan | villas, civic buildings, anything seen from all sides |
| `pyramid` | a hip that comes to points; a square plan gives a single peak | pavilions, towers |
| `mansard` | a steep lower slope (`pitch`, `lower` cells wide) under a shallow upper one (`upperPitch`, default half) | French or Second Empire roofs, a full storey in the roof, dormers |
| `gambrel` | gable wings with two pitches | barns, Dutch colonial |
| `flat-parapet` | a flat deck, a parapet (`parapet` courses) of the wall block, and slab coping | shops, offices, modern buildings |
| `shed` | one slope (the `low` side), with the high side walled | lean-tos, extensions, industrial buildings |
| `dutch-gable` | a hip with small gablets set back at the ridge ends (`inset`) | farmhouses, East Asian roofs |

## Options

- **`pitch`**:
  - `half`: slab steps, about 27°
  - `45`: stairs, 1:1
  - `steep`: stairs with full blocks, 2:1
  - `very-steep`: 3:1
  - or any number (rise per cell)

  Eaves never drop more than one course per cell, so a steep roof does not swallow the top of the wall.
- **`overhang`** 0–2 (default 1). **`eave`**:
  - `plain`
  - `flared`: a half-pitch kick at the eave
  - `cornice`: a course of upside-down `trim` stairs under the eave, with dentils of alternating `trim` blocks under that

  `soffit: true` (or a material) puts top slabs under a plain overhang.
- **Materials**:
  - `material` (the roof; any form of the name works: `deepslate_tiles`, `deepslate_tile`, `spruce`)
  - `trim` (cornice, dentils, tower band)
  - `gable` (the gable-end wall; default: the walls' own block)
  - `verge` (the barge course over each gable end)
  - `hips` (the hip stairs)
  - `pattern: {material, every, offset}` (banded courses)
- **`ridge`**:
  - `slab` (default for 45° and steeper): a half slab on the ridge
  - `wall`: a joined wall
  - `crest`: joined iron bars, the Victorian ridge crest
  - `rods`: end rods every other cell
  - `none`
  - or any block
- **`dormers`**: `{face, count | every, style: gable|shed|eyebrow, width (3), height (2), window, wall}`. Dormers are
  placed symmetrically on that face of the largest wing, keep clear of hip ends and the pediment, and step down or
  drop out where the main roof doesn't rise over them within four rows (so they never tunnel through it).
- **`pediment`**: `{face, width (55% of the face), pitch (45), tympanum, cornice (raking cornice material), oculus
  (true), depth}`, or just `"north"`. This is a classical cross-gable over the front half of that face, with its
  gable filled with `tympanum`, a raking cornice, and a small round window in the middle.
- **`chimneys`**: `[{at: [x,z], size, material, rise}]`. A chimney rises `rise` (2) above the roof top. A 1x1 chimney
  gets a smoking campfire on top, and bigger ones get slab caps.
- **`tower`**: `{at: [x,z], size (n or [w,d]), height (above the roof top), top: lantern|spire|cap, material}`. This
  is a hollow shaft through the roof with a band and small openings near the top, finished with one of:
  - `lantern`: corner posts, iron-bar railings, a hanging lantern, a small pyramid cap and a lightning-rod finial
  - `spire`: a 3:1 pyramid
  - `cap`: slab coping
- **`monitor`** (gable styles): a louvred vent along the middle 60% of the ridge. **`gableCornice`**: the cornice
  also runs across the gable ends (the base of a pediment). **`dentils: false`**: a slim cornice. **`rail`**
  (flat-parapet): iron bars along the coping.
- **`keep`**: `[{from:[x,y,z], to:[x,y,z]}]`, cells never written or removed (a chimney or tower you want to keep).
  Functional cells (redstone, doors and the rest) are always protected. `grow` (default true) grows the grid to fit
  overhangs and height; the result's `shift` says how far everything moved.

## Re-roofing an existing build

`reroof` and `mcd roof` work in three steps:
1. **Find the walls.** Tall columns are walls; the holes between them are filled to get the plan.
2. **Find the eave.** Each perimeter column's wall top is its highest solid with a mostly solid column beneath
   (stairs and slabs at the top count as roof). The eave is the most common wall top.
3. **Find the footprint.** Columns that reach the eave band form it, so a low porch drops out. It is cleaned up
   (one-cell notches filled, one-cell pilasters and buttresses dropped), split into rectangles, and keep boxes are
   cut out.

Then it removes everything above the eave over the footprint (+3 for old overhangs), plus old eave stairs and slabs,
and builds the style. Check `--detect` first. If the footprint is wrong, pass `--footprint x0,z0,x1,z1;...` and
`--y`.

## Choosing a roof that matches a concept

- **Roof height**: a steep hip over a 16-wide plan rises 16 blocks, which is taller than most concepts show. For
  "steep slate" on a wide building, use a **mansard** (`pitch: steep`, `lower: 3`): it reads as a steep roof from
  the street, and the shallow top holds the crest.
- **A front pediment** turns a plain roof into a civic one. Use `cornice` in an accent material (oak reads as gilt
  against slate) and `eave: cornice` on the main roof.
- **Towers** read best small. An elevator head is the shaft's front 4x5 and one storey above the roof, not the whole
  shaft.

The worked example is `examples/roofs/deepslate.mjs`, which re-roofs Deepslate Holdings to match its concept.
`examples/roofs/deepslate-compare.png` shows the concept, before and after.

# Landscaping: the site as code

A building sits on a site, and the site is half the design. Fallingwater is a house cantilevered over a waterfall,
anchored on horizontal sandstone ledges, with a boulder coming up through the hearth, in woods. Build the site with
**brushes** in a generator script, the way you build massing with shape brushes. You decide where things go; each
brush is deterministic (the same arguments give the same blocks) and natural by construction. The brushes are in
`tools/src/terrain.mjs` and exported through `build.mjs`.

```js
import { Grid, heightfield, strata, boulder, stream, waterfall, tree, woods, path, bridge, groundAt } from "<plugin>/tools/src/build.mjs";
```

The working example is `examples/landscape/make.mjs`: a 60x30x50 wooded valley with a 4-block fall over a ledge,
a path, a footbridge, and a stand-in house of cantilevered trays. `examples/landscape/sheet.png` shows the result.
Coordinates are x east, y up, z south. **Order matters**: terrain, then strata, then water, then rocks, then the
building, then paths and bridges, then woods (so trees avoid what is already there).

## The brushes

| brush | example | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `heightfield(g, heights, opts)` | `heightfield(g, (x, z) => 13 + Math.abs(x - 30) * 0.4 + fbm(x/9, 0, z/9, 4) * 4)` | `heights` can be a `[z][x]` array, a `fn(x,z)` or `heightsFromPng(png, {width, depth, min, max})`. It writes the top block plus `depth` (default 3) blocks under it, down to the lowest neighbour on steep faces, so files stay small. Topsoil by slope: 3+ is bare `rock`, 2 is coarse dirt. Ground in shade (`shade(x,z)` above 0.5) gets podzol and moss; elsewhere grass with sparse coarse-dirt patches. Returns `surface(x,z)`. |
| `strata(g, {from, to}, opts)` | `strata(g, {from:[16,7,6], to:[45,16,23]}, {open:["south"]})` | Horizontal sedimentary ledges. Courses are 1–3 thick and alternate hard and soft. Hard courses reach the edge as a lip; soft courses step back `recess` (1, sometimes 2). Edges are jagged by `jag` along the `open` sides, and cells stepped back are carved to air. `rock`: `"pennsylvania"` (default: grey stone and andesite lips over tuff and rubbly cobblestone; this reads as Bear Run sandstone), `"sandstone"`, `"grey"`, `"deepslate"`, or `{hard:[...], soft:[...], cap}`. Returns `courses`. |
| `boulder(g, centre, size, opts)` | `boulder(g, [33,19,15], [2,2,1.6], {flatTop:true, moss:0})` | A noise-displaced ellipsoid (`amount` 0.3), with moss on upward faces (`moss` 0.35). `flatTop` cuts it at 40% of its height: a hearth stone or a table rock. |
| `stream(g, points, opts)` | `stream(g, [[30,0,5],[33,22,5]], {level:16})` | A bed along `[x,z]` or `[x,z,width]` points with the water surface at `level`, `depth` 2 (shallower at the edges), a gravel and sand bed, and banks one above the water. Banks mix gravel, mossy cobble, coarse dirt and mud, with moss carpet and ferns. Ends are flat, and only `clear` (4) blocks above the water are cut, so a reach can meet a fall or a cliff. **Sources only, sealed on every side.** |
| `waterfall(g, opts)` | `waterfall(g, {lip:[32,16,23], dir:"south", drop:4, width:4, pool:{radius:4, depth:2}})` | `lip` is the water cell at the ledge edge. Each column gets a lip source, one level-1 cell out over the edge, level-8 (falling) water down to the plunge pool, and solid rock behind. Start the lower reach **inside** the pool, or the two touch only diagonally (a broken stream). |
| `tree(g, at, species, size, seed)` | `tree(g, [10, 14, 8], "oak", 1.2, 3)` | `oak` (branches, 3–4 crown lobes), `birch` (tall, narrow), `dark_oak` (2x2, root flare, layered crown), `spruce` (alternating rings; a stand-in for hemlock), `azalea` (a rhododendron-like shrub with flowering leaves). Leaves are `persistent=true`, so they do not decay when placed. Trees write only into air or plants. |
| `woods(g, {from, to}, opts)` | `woods(g, {from:[0,0], to:[59,49]}, {density:0.032, mix:{oak:3, birch:2, dark_oak:1, spruce:1}, understory:0.025, avoid:[HOUSE], avoidCells:pathCells})` | Poisson-spaced trees (`spacing` 4.5), with `clumping` 0.35 leaving clearings so they gather into groves, plus an azalea understory. Trees grow only on soil, stand `water` (3) cells back from water, keep trunks `clearance` (4) from every `avoid` box (no leaf ever inside one), and stay off `avoidCells`. |
| `path(g, points, opts)` | `path(g, [[3,33],[12,38],[21,43]], {width:2, endY:deckY})` | Follows the ground. Steps are smoothed to at most 1 by cutting or filling, each rise gets a stair facing up the slope (`stairs` "cobblestone"), headroom is cleared, and the surface is `material` ("dirt_path"). `startY`/`endY` pin the ends to meet a bridge deck or a door. |
| `bridge(g, from, to, opts)` | `bridge(g, [21,14,43], [31,14,43], {width:3})` | A deck (`spruce_planks`) on log beams, `parapet` fences along both sides, and `abutment` rock under the ends down to the ground. |

`groundAt(g, x, z)` gives the top ground block of a column (ignoring plants, leaves, logs and water); use it to
stand things on the terrain.

## Water that works when placed

Still reaches are source blocks only, and `containWater` (run by both water brushes) seals every water cell's
open sides and underside, so nothing spreads when the structure is placed. A fall is written in the state the
game settles into: lip source, then a level-1 cell over the edge, then level-8 falling cells, then pool sources.
On placement the game recomputes the same blocks. The renderer draws water translucent, with source surfaces at
14/16, flowing cells at (8 − level)/9 and falling water as full-height sheets.

## Check the site

```
mcd check site.nbt --site site.json
```
`site.json` = `{ inflow:[x,y,z], outflow:[x,y,z], building:{from,to}, piers:[[x,z]...], paths:[[[x,z]...]...] }`. It
checks:
- **Water validity**: every water cell is a source, a fed flowing cell, or falling water with water above, and no
  water will spill sideways into air.
- **Continuity**: the stream connects inflow to outflow, 6-connected through the fall.
- **The building**: no water inside or touching its interior air, and no logs or leaves inside its box.
- **Piers on rock**: the block under each pier, or under every column of the bottom layer, is rock. A heightfield
  is only a skin, so a building must stand on strata or boulders.
- **Every path walkable**: steps of at most 0.6 (the player's auto-step; a stair counts as both of its heights),
  with two cells of headroom.

## Look at it like a visitor

Helpers are in `vocab.mjs`. Never a coloured full block standing in for an object.

## The farmhouse (x=1..15, z=11..19)
- [ ] **E1 Rough stone walls.** Cobblestone/stone/andesite/mossy-cobblestone mixed per cell (`wallBlock`/`stoneFill`), cobblestone plinth course at y=1, stone-brick quoins up the four corners. x=1..15, z=11..19, y=1..7. P1.

P1 (walls) + make.sh (roof).
- [ ] **E3 Shuttered windows.** Each opening in `OPENINGS`: glass panes connected along the wall, a stone-brick lintel and jambs (frameCells, P1), a stone-brick-slab sill, and a pair of OPEN `warped_trapdoor` shutters flat against the wall either side (trapdoor open=true, facing the wall). Front: x=4,12 (y3-4) + door x=8 + upper x=4,8,12 (y7); back: x=4,8,12 + upper x=4,8,12; west gable z=15 (y3-4, y7); east z=13,17 (y3-4). `window()`. P2 (gaps left by P1).
- [ ] **E4 Brick chimney.** A 2x2 `bricks` stack at x=9..10, z=14..15 rising out of the ridge to y=14 (made by `mcd roof`, `chimneys` in roof.json), continuing the interior breast of bricks x=9..10, z=14..15, y=2..7 (P1). Hearth niche at (10,2..3,15).

- [ ] **E6 Timber porch / lean-to on the garden side.** Dark-oak posts x=18 (z=12,14,16,18; y=2..3), dark-oak beam y=4 along z, spruce-stair lean-to roof rising west to the house wall (19,4)->(16,7), planks floor at y=1 (x=16..18, z=12..18), spruce rails, entrance gap at z=15, hanging lanterns, a bench, barrel, pot. P2.
- [ ] **E7 Doors and steps.** Front door (8,2..3,11) oak door facing north with a stone-brick slab step + landing; east door (15,2..3,15) onto the porch; porch steps `cobblestone_stairs` (19,1,15). `door()`. P2.
- [ ] **E8 Lanterns on the house.** Two lamp posts by the front door (6,1,10),(10,1,10) (`lamp`), two hanging lanterns under the porch beam (18,3,13),(18,3,17) (`lantern(..., true)`). P2.
- [ ] **E31 Floors and partitions.** Ground floor `spruce_planks` y=1, upper floor `oak_planks` y=5 with the stairwell open at (2,5,14..16); partition wall x=9 with doorways at (9,2..3,13) and (9,6..7,13). P1.

## The interior (see plan.md for coordinates)
- [ ] **E20 Staircase.** Oak stairs facing south along x=2: (2,2,13),(2,3,14),(2,4,15),(2,5,16); fence rail (3,6,14),(3,6,15),(2,6,13). P5.

- [ ] **E25 Interior light.** Lanterns hung over tables, standing on barrels in the bedrooms. P5.

input.concept_subject: A French-country farmstead seen from the street at the north: on the left a two-storey farmhouse of rough mixed grey fieldstone (cobblestone, stone, andesite, a little mossy cobble) on a cobblestone plinth, with pale stone-brick quoins, jambs, lintels and sills, a steep 45-degree red clay-tile gable roof with flared eaves and a ridge along the street, and a tall 2x2 red-brick chimney rising from the ridge's centre. Three bays on the front: shuttered windows either side of a plank front door with a stone step and two lantern posts, three smaller windows above under the eaves, every window flanked by open blue-green (verdigris) shutters. On the garden (east) side a dark-oak-post timber lean-to porch with a spruce-stair roof sloping up to the house wall, hanging lanterns, rails and a bench, with steps down to a gravel yard path. A rough-stone garden wall with a slab cap, the same stone as the house, encloses the potager to the right of the house; a lantern-topped stone-brick gate with a wooden gate leads in from the porch. Inside, a symmetrical kitchen garden: two gravel paths with brick centre lines cross at a stone-brick well with four dark-oak posts, a chain and bucket and a small pyramid roof; four raised beds edged in spruce boards, each with four rows of ripe wheat, carrots, potatoes and beetroots and a small water pool; two flowering rose arches over the main path; fruit trees trained flat against the walls as logs with fanned leaves and blossom; a sundial and a stone urn at the ends of the axis; dark-oak lamp posts with lanterns at the crossing. At the back of the garden, a glass glasshouse with a stepped glass roof and birch frame, a low cold frame of glass panes on a plank frame, and a small spruce tool shed with a dark gabled roof. In front a low picket fence, a gravel path to the door lined with roses, lilac, and a low hedge, and behind the house an orchard of apple trees and a woodpile.
